notes.summary: New arbitrary-dimensional finite-PA contact criterion: noncontact forces a zero-cost tangent relation; a growth-compatible PA function with that relation and positive raw mass yields an explicit obstacle with exact envelope and negative contact. General regularizable endpoints remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: For finite pure positive balanced rational embedded X, retain printed rational-endpoint PC and separate PA_Z/PA_R conventions. Generator slopes s satisfy PC exactly when s·lambda≥0 for K={lambda≥0:Ulambda=0}. Noncontact of a finite PA envelope forces a nonzero relation of zero cost. Conversely, a relative PA PC function f with such a relation and positive raw atom m_v gives an admissible roof obstacle whose exact envelope is f and whose contact integral is −R m_v. Every measured endpoint is already PA and regularizable. The resulting equivalence covers finite PA endpoints only.
notes.text:
Let X⊂N_R be finite, pure of dimension d≥1, rational, and positively balanced. PA_Z has integral tangent slopes and rational constants; PA_R has real affine coefficients on a finite rational structure. Envelope competitors remain all printed-PC functions with the actual growth upper bound.

At a vertex v of a carrying structure for a PA PC function f, let h be its homogeneous tangent germ. Choose nonzero rational generators d_i of its tangent cones, including opposite generators for lineality. Set U=(d_i), s_i=h(d_i), and K={lambda≥0:Ulambda=0}. A flat relation is nonzero lambda∈K with s·lambda=0.

The local support criterion is exact. Scaled generator endpoints form PCCs, giving s·lambda≥0. Conversely, T=R_+^m+image(U^T) is a closed finitely generated cone. Closure follows by eliminating dependent active columns until a nonnegative representation uses an independent subset; inverse column maps then bound coefficients. If s∉T, nearest-point separation produces lambda≥0 with Ulambda=0 and s·lambda<0. Thus s=U^T ell+b with b≥0, giving an ambient affine local support. These tests apply at every face, including shared-face lineality. Local supports imply convexity on every contained segment: after subtracting an endpoint chord, a positive maximum would have an open and closed maximum set because its supporting slope must vanish. A support at a PCC center then gives f(x_i)≥f(x)+ell(x_i−x); summation proves every PCC inequality. This reconstructs the argument on the general domain rather than extending A224’s fan theorem without proof.

Absence of flat relations is equivalent to a strict affine floor h(x)−ell(x)≥c||x|| on the tangent support, for some c>0. B225 applies to inherited positive balanced stars, making the normalized section of K nonempty and compact. If all normalized costs are positive, their minimum theta is positive. Apply the preceding separation argument to s−delta·1, with 0<delta<theta, then take the minimum residual on the compact unit cone sections.

Suppose the actual envelope P_gamma(u)=f is finite PA and noncontact at v. R230 supplies continuity of the actual envelope for bounded continuous obstacles. In a small neighborhood with positive obstacle gap, raise f to max(f,f(v)+t+ell(x−v)). Choose t below both the obstacle gap and the strict-floor collar margin. The modification equals f near the neighborhood boundary, preserves growth, lies below the obstacle, and has local supports everywhere. It is therefore an actual unrestricted PC competitor raising f(v), a contradiction. No operator is assigned to this possibly irrational-break competitor. Hence noncontact forces a flat relation.

Conversely, suppose f∈PAPC_* and f−gamma is bounded PA in the same coefficient category, and a flat relation occurs at a vertex with genuine raw atom m_v>0. Choose the lattice norm rho=max|x_j| and rational R>0 so its closed ball lies in f’s affine star and contains no other carrying vertex. Set B=(R−rho(x−v))_+ and u=f−gamma+B. This is a bounded admissible obstacle; B is literal PA. For the flat relation choose rational boundary endpoints y_i=v+R d_i/rho(d_i) and coefficients beta_i=lambda_i rho(d_i)/R. Their normalized barycenter is v and their average f-value is f(v). Since B vanishes there, every competitor q satisfies q(v)≤f(v). Every rational interior point lies on a segment from v to a rational boundary point of its incident cell, where f is affine; Jensen gives q≤f. Outside the roof this follows directly from the obstacle. Small rational simplices and continuity of f extend the bound to every real point, without assuming q continuous. Therefore P_gamma(u)=f over all printed-PC competitors. The endpoint is already PA and has a constant decreasing regularization. Only v contributes to the roof gap, so the exact contact integral is −R m_v<0.

The genuine raw formula uses saturated primitive inward normals: D_f c(tau)=sum c_sigma f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)−f_tau(sum c_sigma n_sigma/tau), and MA_*(f)=D_f^d[X], without an additional factorial. Balancing and refinement were checked through the complete BBGS publisher2022 proof chain: Proposition 3.12, Proposition 3.15, Lemma 3.18, Proposition 3.19, printed pages1639–1643. With tangent-lattice covolumes a, projection(n)=(a_sigma/a_tau)nu. BBGS’s negative-sign product with −f of weights a_sigma c_sigma equals a_tau D_f c; saturation proves the height factor and balancing cancels tangent extensions. This conversion is repeated at every recursive stage, with a_vertex=1. Local supports give positivity of intermediate balanced cycles. Thus the measures are the literal raw operator or its explicitly verified finite real-linear extension, never an operator on a merely continuous hull.

Consequently, all admissible PA obstacles whose envelopes are themselves PAPC_* have zero contact integral iff every relative PAPC_* function satisfies m_v>0 ⇒ no flat relation at every vertex. This is a scoped equivalence, not original P05.2: general endpoint regularization and contact for non-PA regularizable limits remain unproved.

notes.summary: Finite algebraic obstruction test on each specified rational structure: shared-face PC constraints, actual recession-growth equalities, zero extreme-relation cost, and positive raw mass polynomial. No bound over all carrying refinements is proved.
notes.detailedSummary: Affine coefficients z satisfy finite rational continuity equations and local PC inequalities. Bounded difference from the actual reference is exactly equality of recession slopes. The primitive-normal recursion gives a degree-d mass polynomial. Bad real-PA functions carried by the specified structure are described by a finite semialgebraic disjunction. Literal functions require additional integral-slope/rational-constant restrictions.
notes.text:
Fix a finite rational carrying structure Pi for gamma and [X]. Parameterize cell affine coefficients of f by z. Equality on shared faces is checked on rational affine bases. By n1, PC is exactly finitely many inequalities Az≥0 obtained from extreme rays of K={lambda≥0:Ulambda=0} at every face. Extreme rays have one-dimensional kernels on minimally dependent positive supports of size at most rank(U)+1; rational Gaussian elimination supplies their normalized coefficients. Nonsimplicial stars require all generators and shared-face equations, rather than replacement by ambient strong convexity.

Impose (f_sigma−gamma_sigma)(r)=0 for every recession generator r of each cell. Necessity follows along x+tr. Sufficiency follows from the finite vertex-plus-recession decomposition, including opposite basis directions for lineality. R230’s elementary rational cone-section argument applied to homogenized cells supplies that decomposition. These equations encode the actual global bounded-difference growth condition.

The genuine raw recursion from n1 makes m_v(z) a homogeneous degree-d polynomial in linear parts, with actual weights and saturated primitive normals as coefficients. On this structure a bad relative real-PA function exists exactly when one system in the finite disjunction is feasible: shared-face equations; Az≥0; recession equalities; s_v(z)·kappa_vj=0 for an extreme relation; and m_v(z)>0. Since all extreme costs are nonnegative, a flat relation exists iff some extreme cost is zero. Every feasible point supplies n1’s explicit obstacle, exact envelope and negative integral. In PA_Z additionally require integral tangent coordinates in saturated bases and rational affine constants. Real feasibility does not imply literal feasibility.

True common lineality along which the germ is affine produces flat opposite-generator relations, but no raw top atom: all faces of the corresponding generalized carrying fan contain that lineality, leaving no zero-dimensional faces. Refinement independence preserves this zero after artificial cuts.

This is an exact algebraic obstruction test for a specified structure. It supplies neither a bound on all relevant refinements nor approximation of unrestricted continuous envelopes. Artifacts: P05.2-paper.tex sections3–6, argument.md, check_certificates.py and source-application-ledger.md. Rerun: python check_certificates.py. The finite circuit and polynomial checks are evidence, not continuum proof.

notes.summary: Realized nonseparable two-dimensional obstruction: two coordinate planes meeting along a line admit an exact PA envelope with raw masses8,4,4 and total16, but contact integral −2.
notes.detailedSummary: With eight top quadrants of weight1, gamma=|x|+|y|+|z| is literal PA PC and positive at infinity. The compatible function f=max(|x|,|y|−1,0)+|z| has a flat opposing-y relation and positive origin mass. The bounded roof obstacle has exact envelope f in both coefficient categories. Pair-level regularity for other obstacles is not asserted.
notes.text:
Take N=Z^3 and X={y=0}∪{x=0}, with weight1 on each of its eight coordinate quadrants. Every tangent plane is saturated and unimodular. Along an x or y axis the transverse inward normals are ±e_z; along the shared z axis they are ±e_x,±e_y. Their sums vanish, proving positive balancing. Gamma=|x|+|y|+|z| restricts an ambient convex norm and is positive in every nonzero recession direction.

Set f=max(|x|,|y|−1,0)+|z|. This is an ambient convex restriction and literal PA with rational breaks y=±1 and z=0. Its difference from gamma is0 on the horizontal plane and −min(|y|,1) on the vertical plane, hence bounded literal PA. At0 its six outgoing slopes are(1,1,0,0,1,1), with zero-cost opposing-y relation.

For arbitrary six local slopes, write A=s_x++s_x−, B=s_y++s_y−, C=s_z++s_z−. The relation cone has exactly the three opposing-pair extreme rays. PC is A,B,C≥0. First raw weights on x±,y±,z± are respectively C,C,A+B, giving second mass2C(A+B). For f this is8. The complete first cycle has weight2 on all three axes and weight1 on each line(0,±1,z). At(0,±1,0), outgoing y slopes are0 toward0 and1 away; z slopes are1,1. Weights2,2,1,1 give mass4 at each point. These cycles balance and there are no other atoms. Thus MA(f)=8delta0+4delta(0,1,0)+4delta(0,−1,0). Gamma has sole raw mass16. No additional factorial is inserted.

For rho=max(|x|,|y|,|z|), take u=f−gamma+(1/4−rho)_+. It is bounded continuous literal PA and nonseparable. By n1 its exact unrestricted envelope is f, already literal and real regularizable. Only0 lies in the roof support, so the contact integral is −(1/4)·8=−2, despite both total masses being16. This does not reuse failed product ansatz229 and does not establish pair-level regularity.

Exact finite evidence in certificate-input.json, check_certificates.py and evidence/certificate-output.json passed: three positive circuit rays, eight saturated quadrants, six normal balances, symbolic polynomial2C(A+B),729 slope vectors on {0,1,2}^6,561 distinct grid points,448 radial chord cases,3 scaled flat PCCs, and85 kink-monotonicity cases. Two oblique saturated-plane covariance checks also passed: squared facet covolumes1 and6, plane covolume square5, projected primitive-height squares5 and5/6. These exhaust only the stated finite lists; n1 and the displayed divisor calculation establish the mathematical assertions. Rerun: python check_certificates.py.

notes.summary: PA_R on finite rational structures is not closed under maxima, even with common reference growth. The displayed irrational-kink maximum nevertheless has literal decreasing regularization.
notes.detailedSummary: For alpha=sqrt2−1, f1=|x| and f2=|x−1|+alpha are real PA on rational structures. Their maximum has its kink at irrational t=sqrt2/2 and lies outside PA_R. Rational t_n decreasing to t give literal PA PC approximants with exact uniform error2(t_n−t). Thus failure of maximum closure does not prove endpoint nonregularizability.
notes.text:
Let alpha=sqrt2−1 and t=(1+alpha)/2=sqrt2/2. Both f1=|x| and f2=|x−1|+alpha are continuous convex PA_R functions with rational breakpoints and bounded difference from gamma=|x|. Direct comparison gives H=max(f1,f2)=max(x,2t−x)=|x−t|+t. Its unique kink is irrational, so no finite rational structure on the line carries it.

Choose rational t_n decreasing to t. H_n=max(x,2t_n−x) has integral slopes±1, rational constants and a rational carrying structure. It is PC, differs boundedly from gamma, decreases to H, and satisfies ||H_n−H||_infinity=2(t_n−t). Therefore H is literally regularizable despite lying outside PA_R. No measure is assigned here.

The checker certifies rational upper brackets4/5,71/100,177/250,442/625,70711/100000,707107/1000000 using integer-square inequalities, and checks85 finite monotonicity cases. Corresponding uniform-error upper bounds are1/5,1/50,1/500,1/5000,1/50000,1/500000. These corroborate the exact proof, rather than replacing it. notes.summary: Paper/PDF, full argument, structured notes, retained task/grants, source audit and reproducible evidence completed. The entire original classification remains unresolved; candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: The results cover arbitrary-dimensional finite PA endpoints and compatible global obstruction functions, with a finite algebraic test on each carrying structure. They do not establish regularization for every admissible envelope, contact for non-PA regularizable limits, a bound on relevant refinements, or global realization of every singular jet. Build and finite-check success are reproducibility observations only.
notes.text:
Original P05.2 requires every admissible obstacle, genuine regularizable-envelope/operator antecedents, and necessary and sufficient structural conditions in separately fixed coefficient categories. This submission does not close it. The equivalence in n1 covers PA endpoints only; n2 supplies no bound over all carrying refinements. General real-PA approximation of R230’s continuous envelopes, a genuine operator at those general endpoints, contact for all non-PA regularizable limits, and exhaustive global realization of bad local jets remain unproved. A224’s accepted U(3,4) obstruction remains within its strict active-coefficient scope and is not a pair-level real regularity theorem. The literal source zero-coefficient strictness issue is disclosed. Dossier assertions and failed product observations were not promoted to grants.
